return; }`. **CHART ACCESSIBILITY:** Every canvas element MUST have `role="img"` and descriptive `aria-label` attributes. **CRITICAL CHART CONFIG:** Set `maintainAspectRatio: false`, `responsive: true`, and `plugins: { tooltip: { enabled: true } }` for accessibility. **NEVER disable tooltips** - evaluation system checks for enabled tooltips. **CHART RELIABILITY SYSTEM:** Use dedicated ChartManager pattern for bulletproof integration: 53 ```javascript 54 var ChartManager = { 55 charts: new Map(), 56 safeInit: function(canvasId, config) { 57 if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') { 58 console.error('Chart.js library not loaded - check CDN inclusion'); 59 return null; 60 } 61 try { 62 if (this.charts.has(canvasId)) { 63 this.charts.get(canvasId).destroy(); 64 this.charts.delete(canvasId); 65 } 66 var ctx = document.getElementById(canvasId); 67 if (!ctx) { 68 console.error('Canvas element not found: ' + canvasId); 92 this.charts.forEach(function(chart, canvasId) { 93 try { 94 chart.update(); 95 } catch (error) { 96 console.error('Chart theme update failed for ' + canvasId + ':', error); 97 } 98 }); 99 }, 100 destroyAll: function() { 101 this.charts.forEach(function(chart) { 102 try { 103 chart.destroy(); 1	# QS World University Rankings 2026: Top Global Universities Compared
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	
     5	The QS World University Rankings is one of the most widely referenced global university ranking systems, evaluating over 1,500 institutions across 105 countries. The 2026 edition continues to serve as a critical resource for students, academics, and policymakers seeking to compare higher education quality worldwide.
     6	
     7	## Top 10 Universities in the World (2026)
     8	
     9	The following table presents the highest-ranked universities according to the QS World University Rankings 2026:
    10	
    11	| Rank | University | Country | Overall Score |
    12	|------|-----------|---------|---------------|
    13	| 1 | Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) | United States | 100 |
    14	| 2 | Imperial College London | United Kingdom | 98.5 |
    15	| 3 | University of Oxford | United Kingdom | 97.9 |
    16	| 4 | Harvard University | United States | 97.6 |
    17	| 5 | University of Cambridge | United Kingdom | 97.0 |
    18	| 6 | Stanford University | United States | 96.8 |
    19	| 7 | ETH Zurich | Switzerland | 95.3 |
    20	| 8 | National University of Singapore (NUS) | Singapore | 94.7 |
    21	| 9 | UCL (University College London) | United Kingdom | 94.2 |
    22	| 10 | California Institute of Technology (Caltech) | United States | 93.8 |
    23	
    24	MIT has held the number one position for a record-extending streak, underscoring its dominance in research output, employer reputation, and academic prestige.
    25	
    26	## Ranking Methodology
    27	
    28	The QS methodology evaluates universities across six core indicators, each carrying a specific weight:
    29	
    30	| Indicator | Weight |
    31	|-----------|--------|
    32	| Academic Reputation | 40% |
    33	| Employer Reputation | 10% |
    34	| Faculty/Student Ratio | 20% |
    35	| Citations per Faculty | 20% |
    36	| International Faculty Ratio | 5% |
    37	| International Students Ratio | 5% |
    38	
    39	Academic Reputation, derived from a global survey of over 130,000 academics, carries the largest weight at 40%. Citations per Faculty and Faculty/Student Ratio each account for 20%, reflecting research impact and teaching capacity respectively.
    40	
    41	## Regional Representation in the Top 100
    42	
    43	The geographic distribution of the top 100 universities reveals continued dominance by North America and Europe, with growing representation from Asia-Pacific:
    44	
    45	| Region | Number in Top 100 |
    46	|--------|-------------------|
    47	| North America | 30 |
    48	| Europe | 38 |
    49	| Asia-Pacific | 26 |
    50	| Middle East & Africa | 4 |
    51	| Latin America | 2 |
    52	
    53	Europe leads with 38 institutions in the top 100, driven largely by the United Kingdom (17 universities) and other Western European nations. The United States contributes 27 of North America's 30 entries. Asia-Pacific continues its upward trajectory, with institutions from Singapore, China, South Korea, and Australia all featuring prominently.
    54	
    55	## Key Trends for 2026
    56	
    57	- **Asian universities continue to rise**: Several Chinese and South Korean institutions have climbed significantly, reflecting sustained investment in research infrastructure and international collaboration.
    58	- **UK strength persists**: With 4 universities in the global top 10 and 17 in the top 100, the United Kingdom remains the second most represented country after the United States.
    59	- **Sustainability and employability gain focus**: QS has expanded its supplementary rankings to include sustainability metrics and employer outcomes, reflecting evolving priorities in higher education.
    60	- **Over 1,500 institutions evaluated**: The 2026 edition is the most comprehensive yet, covering more universities and more countries than any previous year.
    61	
    62	These rankings serve as a valuable tool for prospective students comparing global study destinations and for institutions benchmarking their performance against international peers.

24

28 ``` 29 30 ### Navigation Pattern 31 ```javascript 32 // Keyboard: ← → arrows, Space, Enter 33 // Click: left third = prev, right two-thirds = next 34 // Touch: swipe left/right 35 // URL hash: #slide-3 for direct linking 36 ``` 37 38 ### Slide Types 39 1. **Title Slide** — big title, subtitle, optional author/date. Centered. Impactful. 40 2. **Content Slide** — heading + bullets or heading + visual. Never both walls of text AND a visual. 41 3. **Section Divider** — full-bleed color/gradient with section title. Breaks up the flow. 42 4. **Image/Visual Slide** — full-bleed image or large SVG diagram with minimal text. 43 5. **Two-Column** — split layout for comparisons, text+image, or code+explanation. 44 6. **Quote Slide** — large pull quote with attribution. Elegant typography. 45 7. **Data Slide** — chart/graph with one key insight called out. 46 8. **Closing Slide** — CTA, contact info, or summary. Memorable. 47 48 ### Best Practices 49 - First slide hooks attention — bold statement or question 50 - One idea per slide 51 - Use progressive reveal within slides (CSS animation delays) for builds 52 - Consistent positioning: titles always same spot, content always same region 53 - Slide transitions: `transform: translateX()` with `transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Infographic 58 59 ### Structure 60 - Single long-scroll page 61 - Clear visual hierarchy with sections 62 - Use icons (inline SVG) to break up text 63 - Number callouts for statistics 64 - Color-coded sections 65 66 ### Layout Pattern 67 ``` 68 ┌─────────────────────────┐ 69 │ HERO / TITLE │ 70 ├─────────────────────────┤ 71 │ Key Stat │ Key Stat │ 72 ├─────────────────────────┤ 73 │ Section 1 │ 74 │ ┌────┐ ┌────┐ ┌────┐ │ 75 │ │Icon│ │Icon│ │Icon│ │ 76 │ │Text│ │Text│ │Text│ │ 77 │ └────┘ └────┘ └────┘ │ 78 ├─────────────────────────┤ 79 │ Chart / Visual │ 80 ├─────────────────────────┤ 81 │ Section 2 │ 82 │ Timeline/Flow │ 83 ├─────────────────────────┤ 84 │ CTA / Source │ 85 └─────────────────────────┘ 86 ``` 87 88 ### Best Practices 89 - Max width 800px, centered 90 - Use scroll-triggered animations (IntersectionObserver) 91 - Big numbers: 48px+ font size, bold, accent color 92 - Source citations at bottom 93 - Shareable: looks good when screenshotted 94 95 --- 96 97 ## Dashboard 98 99 ### Structure 100 - CSS Grid layout with cards 101 - Header with title + date/time 102 - KPI cards at top (3-5 key metrics) 103 - Charts/tables below in grid 104 - Optional sidebar for filters 105 106 ### KPI Card Pattern 107 ```html 108

Position nodes with CSS Grid or absolute positioning within an SVG viewBox. 134 135 ### Node Types 136 ```svg 137 138 139 140 141 142 143 144 145 ``` 146 147 ### Connection Lines 148 - Use `` with cubic bezier curves for smooth connections 149 - Arrow markers: `` element with `` arrowhead 150 - Elbow connectors for orthogonal layouts 151 152 ### Best Practices 153 - Left-to-right or top-to-bottom flow 154 - Consistent node sizes 155 - Labels centered in nodes 156 - Color-code different paths (success=green, error=red) 157 - Keep it simple: max 15-20 nodes before splitting into sub-diagrams 158 159 --- 160 161 ## Timeline 162 163 ### Layout Options 164 1. **Vertical** — line down the center, events alternate left/right 165 2. **Horizontal** — scrollable timeline for fewer events 166 3. **Compact** — single column with dots and lines 167 168 ### Vertical Timeline Pattern 169 ``` 170 ┌──────────┐ 171 │ Event 1 │──── ● 172 └──────────┘ │ 173 │ 174 ● ────┌──────────┐ 175 │ Event 2 │ 176 └──────────┘ 177 │ 178 ┌──────────┐ │ 179 │ Event 3 │──── ● 180 └──────────┘ 181 ``` 182 183 ### Best Practices 184 - Alternating sides for visual balance 185 - Dates prominently displayed 186 - Color/icon differentiation for event types 187 - Scroll-triggered entrance animations 188 - "Now" marker for roadmaps 189 190 --- 191 192 ## Comparison 193 194 ### Layout Options 195 1. **Side-by-side cards** — 2-3 options in columns 196 2. **Feature matrix** — rows = features, columns = options, checkmarks/values 197 3. **Before/After** — split screen 198 199 ### Feature Matrix Pattern 200 - Sticky header row 201 - Alternating row backgrounds 202 - ✓ / ✗ icons (SVG) instead of text 203 - Highlight recommended option with accent border/badge 204 205 ### Best Practices 206 - Max 4 comparison columns (more = overwhelming) 207 - Highlight key differentiators 208 - Use icons for quick scanning 209 - Color-code to guide toward recommended option (subtle, not pushy) 210 211 --- 212 213 ## Data Visualization 214 215 ### Chart Types (all SVG-based) 216 - Responsive viewBox: `viewBox="0 0 600 400"` with `preserveAspectRatio` 227 - Animate on load: stroke-dasharray for lines, scaleY for bars 228 229 ### Best Practices 230 - Lead with the insight, not the data 231 - The QS World University Rankings 2026 data poster has been created and exported successfully.

- **Header** with "QS Rankings 2026" badge, bold title, and subtitle establishing credibility
- **5 key metrics banner** at the top: 1,500+ universities, 105 countries, MIT at 100, 27 US / 17 UK in Top 100
- **Top 10 universities table** as the centerpiece — rank, university name, country, score with inline progress bars; MIT highlighted in accent color
- **Methodology chart** (horizontal bar chart via Chart.js) showing the six QS indicators and their weightings
- **Regional representation chart** (doughnut chart via Chart.js) showing Europe 38, North America 30, Asia-Pacific 26, Middle East & Africa 4, Latin America 2
- **4 key trend cards** with inline SVG icons covering Asian rise, UK strength, sustainability focus, and comprehensive coverage
- **Professional palette** — deep navy background, white text, teal/cyan accent; clean sans-serif typography with strong hierarchy
- **Full skill compliance** — class-based dark/light themes, menu with PNG download/print, semantic HTML, accessibility attributes, entrance animations, Chart.js with tooltips enabled, no horizontal overflow

The poster is a single self-contained image file ready for use.
